about_the_game:
Margin of Error is a roguelike deck-builder fused with math puzzles, where every card you play could lead to triumph… or total failure. Build equations with numbers and operators to defeat enemies, withstand unique debuffs, and climb your way to the highest score. Will you trust your logic or gamble on luck?

BUILD YOUR DECK

You will start with a variety of math cards that appear randomly ranging from numbers 0–9, basic operators like +, –, ×, ÷, to special cards such as π and square roots. Each run can deal you a different combination. At later stages, you can even build formulas shaped like squares, triangles, and even the golden ratio to unleash greater damage.

FACE UNIQUE ENEMIES

Enemies don’t just have HP—they fight back with debuffs that twist your calculations. Every battle feels different.

STAMPS & MODULES

Power up your run with Stamps (permanent buffs) and Modules (situational bonuses). Will you build a stable equation engine, or gamble on high-risk, high-reward combos?

THE GACHA GAMBLE

Between rounds, you’ll face the temptation of gacha. Take the risk for a chance at epic effects or pay the price when luck turns against you. It’s not just math; it’s courage under pressure.

pc_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • OS: Windows 10 (64-bit)
  • Processor: Intel Core i3-2100 (2.0 GHz) or AMD FX-4100 (2.0 GHz)
  • Memory: 4 GB RAM
  • Graphics: DirectX 10 compatible graphics card with 512 MB VRAM
  • Storage: 500 MB available space
  • Sound Card: DirectX compatible sound card
pc_requirements.recommended:
Recommended:
  • OS: Windows 10+ (64-bit)
  • Processor: Intel Core i5-4460 (3.2 GHz) or AMD Ryzen 3 1200 (3.1 GHz)
  • Memory: 8 GB RAM
  • Graphics: DirectX 11 compatible graphics card with 1 GB VRAM
  • Storage: 1 GB available space
  • Sound Card: DirectX compatible sound card

short_description: Margin of Error is a roguelike deck-building game with a mathematical puzzle twist, where you play not just with numbers - but also with logic and strategy. it features a card system with numbers 0-9 and unique operators like +, -, ×, (pi), etc.
